To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TDM is a promising tool to guide treatment decisions in patients with moderate to severe psoriatic arthritis or psoriasis.
TDM of biologics is an emerging tool in the treatment of patients with moderate to severe psoriatic disease.
therapeutic drug monitoring is a useful tool for optimizing the use of biological agents for the treatment of psoriatic disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the practical implementation of TDM in clinical routine.
the clinical utility of TDM in the management of psoriasis and its impact on patient care and costs.
the clinical utility of TDM of biologics, and its potential impact on patient care and healthcare costs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TDM is a valuable tool in clinical practice for patients with psoriasis, but more research is needed to define target therapeutic ranges and to assess the impact of TDM on clinical outcome.
there is a lack of evidence for the routine use of TDM in psoriasis, although the evidence for its utility in patients who lose response is growing.
TDM should be used as a tool to optimize therapy and to improve patient outcomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

TDM is an important tool for clinical decision-making and that it is recommended to perform a therapeutic drug concentration and anti-drug antibody assessment in all patients with psoriasis on biologic therapy, especially in patients who do not respond to treatment.

TDM should be considered in all patients with moderate to severe psoriatic disease and that it should be performed before the initiation of treatment, at least 3 months after the start of treatment and at the time of loss of response to biologic therapy.
TDM should be performed in patients with a poor response to biologic therapy, in patients with a history of non-adherence, in patients who lose response and in cases of suspected immunogenicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TDM of biologics should be considered a routine clinical practice in patients with moderate to severe psoriatic disease.
TDM is a valuable tool for optimizing the use of biologics.
the TDM of biologics has the potential to improve the efficacy of treatment and to reduce costs.
